interest: Shows Senator Vandenberg prompting State to gather Depression-era intelligence on Hokkaido's beet-sugar and pulp industry.
overview: This State Department file (decimal file 894.61353) centers on an inquiry from the American domestic sugar beet and livestock feed industry regarding the nascent export of Japanese beet pulp to the United States. Initiated in early 1935 by the Farmers & Manufacturers Beet Sugar Association and the Larrowe Milling Company through Senator Arthur H. Vandenberg of Michigan, the inquiry prompted Secretary of State Cordell Hull to direct the American Consulate General in Tokyo to compile a detailed economic report. The resulting investigation, prepared by Vice Consul Charles A. Hutchinson, documents the cultivation of sugar beets on the northern island of Hokkaido, the operations of the Hokkaido Seito and Meiji Seito corporations, and initial export shipments of compressed beet pulp handled by Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha to the U.S. Atlantic and Pacific coasts. The file concludes with the transmission of the completed findings back to Senator Vandenberg, alongside an unrelated 1933 Division of Far Eastern Affairs memorandum regarding a Mitsubishi report on the Japanese rubber industry.

subfiles.about: A detailed consular economic report outlining sugar beet cultivation in Hokkaido, factory slicing capacities, domestic pulp consumption, export statistics to the United States, and expansion forecasts.
subfiles.from: Charles A. Hutchinson, American Vice Consul, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Compiled by Vice Consul Charles A. Hutchinson and approved by Consul General Arthur Garrels, this special consular report provides an extensive survey of Japan's sugar beet and pulp industries. Cultivation is concentrated on the northern island of Hokkaido, where two major firms—Hokkaido Seito Kabushiki Kaisha and Meiji Seito Kabushiki Kaisha—operate processing factories and plan additional facilities to double production by 1937. While beet pulp was historically consumed locally as dairy cow feed, surplus production led to export consignments beginning in late 1934, sending over 3,600 long tons to the U.S. Atlantic and Pacific coasts through Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha. An appended statistical table details annual seeded acreage, beet tonnage, refined sugar output, and pulp yields from the 1930–31 season through 1934–35.
subfiles.title: Report No. 137 on Production, Uses, Export, and Expansion of Beet Sugar and Pulp in Japan

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull forwards the Tokyo Consulate General's despatch and special report on Japanese beet pulp to Senator Vandenberg.
subfiles.summary: Hull sends Vandenberg the consular report on Japan's beet sugar and pulp industry, offering further help if needed.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of State Cordell Hull to Senator Arthur H. Vandenberg transmitting consular report
